subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest design should OpenClaw support for core config and auth-profile storage: native OS keychain, master/passphrase sealing, SecretRef-only migration, or a staged combination?
rationale: The implementation choice defines the security boundary, unattended-startup behavior, recovery/rotation model, and upgrade path for existing plaintext credentials, so automation should not choose it.

options.title: Staged core design
options.body: Define a staged design that preserves SecretRefs, adds explicit encrypted-at-rest storage for core-owned credentials, and includes doctor migration plus recovery/rotation docs.

options.title: SecretRef-only policy
options.body: Declare SecretRefs plus OS isolation as the supported at-rest mitigation and close native encryption as out of scope after updating the threat-model and docs language.

options.title: Passphrase sealing first
options.body: Adopt optional passphrase sealing as an interim hardening path, accepting operator-action and unattended-startup tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Staged core design
recommendation.body: Define a staged design that preserves SecretRefs, adds explicit encrypted-at-rest storage for core-owned credentials, and includes doctor migration plus recovery/rotation docs.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available owner signal from merged SecretRef review history plus auth-profile persistence refactor history; the final choice still needs maintainer/security consensus.
